homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today a new liturgical year begins, and our Church begins it in a very wise way: not with Christmas, but with the Church herself. Qudos Eetho, the Sanctification of the Church. Before we celebrate the mysteries of Christ, we remember the house in which we celebrate them.

Listen to the long story told in our readings. Moses sets up the Tabernacle; Solomon builds the Temple; Ezekiel sees the glory of the Lord leave the Temple because the people had defiled it; Isaiah sees the Lord on his throne and hears the seraphim cry, “Holy, holy, holy.” God wants to live among his people, but his holiness can never be taken for granted.

Then St Peter tells us where God lives now: in us. “Like living stones, let yourselves be built into a spiritual house.” Every baptised person is a stone in God's house. Some stones carry weight; some stones crumble. This year, what kind of stone will I be?

And in the Gospel Jesus says to Peter: “On this rock I will build my church.” For us Syro-Malankara Catholics these words are dear. In 1930 Mar Ivanios led our forefathers into communion with the successor of Peter, while keeping our ancient Syriac liturgy. Unity with Peter and love for our own tradition are not two loyalties; they are one Catholic faith.
In a few moments we will sing with the seraphim, “Holy, holy, holy.” Heaven's song in our parish church. Let us begin this year as living stones, holy, united and faithful. Amen.
kids: Children, what is a church built with? Stones and bricks! But God's Church is built with people. You are a living stone in God's house!
And the most important stone is Jesus. He holds everything together. Peter said, “You are the Christ,” and Jesus built his Church on Peter's faith.
This year, be a strong stone: come to Holy Qurbono, help in the parish, and be kind. Let's say together: “I am a living stone for Jesus!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, last Sunday we celebrated the Church as God's holy house. Today, Hudos Eetho, we celebrate the renewal of the Church. Both are true at once: the Church is holy because Christ makes her holy, and she is always in need of renewal because she is made of us, sinners.

Our readings show two dangers. At Sinai the people made a golden calf, a god they could see and control. And the risen Lord says to the Church of Laodicea: “Because you are lukewarm, I will spit you out of my mouth.” The danger of the Church is not only sin, but comfort.

Then Jesus enters the Temple and overturns the tables of the traders. He was not against worship; he was against worship turned into business. And he said: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” He was speaking of his body. Every true renewal of the Church is a return to Christ, crucified and risen.

So where does renewal begin? Not with someone else. With me. With a good Confession, with silence and reverence in church, with a heart that opens when the Lord knocks. “If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in and eat with him.” In a few moments he will do exactly that at this altar. Amen.
kids: Children, what happens if nobody cleans the house for a long time? Dust everywhere! Jesus once went into the Temple and cleaned it, because people had made it a market.
Our hearts are God's house too. We clean them by saying sorry to Jesus and by praying. Jesus says: “I am standing at your door, knocking.” Shall we open the door to him? Let's say: “Come in, Jesus!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today the season of Suboro begins, the season of good news. And where does the good news begin? In the Temple, with an old priest named Zechariah, burning incense while the people pray outside.

Zechariah and Elizabeth were good people. St Luke says they were “righteous before God”. And yet they had no child, and now they were old. How many years they must have prayed! And perhaps they had stopped asking. Then the angel says: “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard.” God had not forgotten. God's answer came late, but not too late.

Zechariah could not believe it at once. “How will I know this? I am an old man.” And God gave him a strange sign: silence. For nine months he could not speak. That silence was a school. When John was born, the first thing Zechariah did with his freed tongue was to praise God.

Perhaps some of us here carry a prayer that God seems not to have answered: for a child, for a job, for a son who has gone away from the Church, for healing. Do not stop. Like Abraham, who “hoped against hope”, keep trusting. And use this season to prepare your heart, as John prepared a people for the Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, do you like waiting? No! Waiting is hard. Zechariah and Elizabeth waited many, many years for a baby.
Then an angel came and said: “God has heard your prayer!” And God gave them a baby called John. John grew up to tell everyone: “Jesus is coming!”
When you pray, God always listens. Sometimes we must wait. Let's say together: “God hears my prayer!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, last Sunday an angel came to an old priest in the great Temple of Jerusalem. Today the same angel goes to a little village called Nazareth, to a young girl named Mary. God's greatest work begins in a small house, in a heart that listens.

Our readings remind us that God had promised this from the very beginning. When Adam and Eve sinned, God said that the offspring of the woman would crush the serpent's head. For centuries the prophets cried, “O that you would tear open the heavens and come down!” And St Paul says, “When the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman.” Today that fullness arrives.

Mary asks a question: “How can this be?” Faith may ask questions. But then she says the words that changed the world: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.” The Fathers said: Eve's disobedience tied a knot; Mary's obedience untied it. Through her, the Son of God became man; that is why we call her Mother of God.

God is still looking for hearts that say yes. Perhaps he asks you to forgive someone, to accept an illness, to give time to prayer, or to answer a call to the priesthood or religious life. In a few moments the Holy Spirit will come down upon this altar as he came upon Mary. Let us say with her: “Let it be with me according to your word.” Amen.
kids: Children, who visited Mary in her little house? The angel Gabriel! He said: “Mary, God is with you. You will have a baby, and you will call him Jesus.”
Mary said: “Yes, I will do what God wants.” And Jesus, God's own Son, became a tiny baby inside her.
Every day God asks us small things: to obey, to share, to pray. Let's say like Mary: “Yes, God!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, what do we do when we receive great news? We pick up the phone and tell someone. When Mary received the greatest news in history, she did something more: she set out and went with haste to the hill country, to help her elderly cousin Elizabeth.

Imagine the scene. Mary greets Elizabeth, and the baby in Elizabeth's womb leaps for joy. John recognises Jesus before either of them is born. Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit, says: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.” Every time we pray the Hail Mary, we repeat her words.

Then Mary sings: “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior.” She does not sing about herself. She sings about a God who looks on the lowly, lifts up the poor, fills the hungry with good things, and sends the proud away empty. Like Hannah before her, she knows that God works through the small and the humble.

On Tuesday the Twenty-Five Days Nombu begins. Let us keep it like Mary: not only by giving up food, but by going out. Visit someone who is old, sick or lonely. Carry Christ to them, as Mary did. And after every Holy Qurbono, remember: you leave this church as Mary left Nazareth, carrying the Lord within you. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary had a cousin called Elizabeth who was going to have a baby. Mary walked a long way over the hills to help her.
When Mary said hello, baby John jumped inside Elizabeth's tummy, because Jesus was there inside Mary! John was so happy.
Before Christmas, let's be like Mary: help someone at home, visit Grandma or Grandpa, and bring Jesus' joy. Let's say: “I will bring Jesus to others!”

homily: Dear friends, the day after the Church was dedicated to God on Qudos Eetho Sunday, Paul tells us plainly what God wants: this is the will of God, your sanctification; God did not call us to impurity but in holiness (1 Thessalonians 4:3, 7). Holiness is not for a few; it is the calling of all the baptised.

In the Beatitudes Jesus paints the portrait of holiness: the poor in spirit, those who mourn, the meek, those who hunger for righteousness, the merciful, the pure in heart, the peacemakers. Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God (Matthew 5:8).

The Beatitudes are the face of the saints. This week choose one of them and try to live it: perhaps meekness, perhaps making peace. We are the living stones of the Church that was dedicated yesterday. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God. Today, only good thoughts and good words!

homily: Dear friends, today the Church celebrates the tradition that Mary, Mother of God, as a little child was brought by her parents Joachim and Anne to the Temple and given to God. The details come from Tradition, not from the Gospels, but their meaning is clear: from the very beginning Mary's whole life was given to God, like Samuel whom Hannah lent to the Lord.

In the Gospel, when Jesus' mother and brothers stand outside, he points to his disciples and says: here are my mother and my brothers! Whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother (Matthew 12:49–50). Mary is Jesus' mother first not in the body but in a heart that received God's will.

Paul says: rejoice in the Lord always; whatever is true, honourable, just and pure, think about these things (Philippians 4:4, 8). This was Mary's heart. Today let us give our day to God with Mary; pray three Hail Marys and place this day in her hands. Amen.
kids: Children, little Mary was given to God. Today you too can say: God, this day is yours!

homily: Dear friends, on this Monday after Hudos Eetho Sunday, Hebrews reads Psalm 95 as a call for today: today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts. Israel in the desert did not enter God's rest because of disobedience; but the promise is still open (Hebrews 4:7–9).

In the Gospel Jesus says: take care that you do not despise one of these little ones; for in heaven their angels continually see the face of my Father. Like a shepherd who goes after one lost sheep, it is not the will of the Father in heaven that one of these little ones should be lost (Matthew 18:10–14).

Today is the day to listen. Do today the conversion, the reconciliation or the prayer you have put off till tomorrow. And let us protect children and the weak, as the angels of God protect them. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said every child has a guardian angel. Pray to your guardian angel today!

homily: Dear friends, today is the feast of Mar Andrews Shleeha, St Andrew the Apostle. Two disciples of John the Baptist hear him say, look, here is the Lamb of God, and follow Jesus. He turns and asks: what are you looking for? Rabbi, where are you staying? Come and see, he says, and they remain with him that day. Andrew first finds his brother Simon and tells him: we have found the Messiah; and he brings him to Jesus (John 1:36–42).

Paul writes to the Galatians with a mother's heart: my little children, for whom I am again in the pain of childbirth until Christ is formed in you (Galatians 4:19). Bringing others to Christ carries the pain of love.

In this week after the Sunday of the Visitation, like Mary who went in haste to Elizabeth, like Andrew who ran to his brother, let us bring Christ to someone. Say to one person: come and see, to a prayer, to a Holy Qurbono. Amen.
kids: Children, when Andrew found Jesus he ran and brought his brother. Tell someone too: come and see!

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews asks us to remember our leaders, those who spoke the word of God to us, and to imitate their faith. Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and for ever (Hebrews 13:7–8). Today the Church remembers the Fathers of the Council of Nicaea (AD 325), whom tradition numbers as 318. They confessed that the Son is of one being with the Father; the Creed we pray at every Holy Qurbono comes from them.

In the Gospel Jesus speaks of the faithful and wise servant whom the master puts in charge of his household: blessed is that servant whom his master will find at work when he arrives (Matthew 24:45–46). The Fathers of Nicaea were such servants; many bore in their bodies the wounds of persecution.
Faith is both an inheritance and a responsibility. This week pray the Creed slowly, meditating on its meaning, and explain one line of it to your children. Amen.
kids: Children, long ago bishops gathered in a city called Nicaea and confessed that Jesus is true God. Today pray the Creed with all your heart!

homily: Dear friends, the Corinthians were proud of their favourite preachers and of their own gifts. Paul brings them down to earth with one question: what do you have that you did not receive? And if you received it, why do you boast as if it were not a gift (1 Corinthians 4:7)? Everything is gift.

Jesus says the same truth another way: do not judge, and you will not be judged; forgive, and you will be forgiven. Why do you see the speck in your neighbour's eye but do not notice the log in your own (Luke 6:37, 41)?

Those who receive everything as gift find it hard to judge others. A practice for today: when you are tempted to criticise someone, first think for a moment about the log in your own eye, then say a short prayer for that person. Amen.
kids: Children, it is easy to find faults in others. Today say only good things about someone!

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews speaks to Christians tired of struggling. Their trials are not a sign that God has abandoned them but that he treats them as sons and daughters: the Lord disciplines those whom he loves (Hebrews 12:6). Discipline is painful at the time, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness.

In the Gospel Jesus reveals his relationship with the Father: the Son can do nothing on his own, but only what he sees the Father doing; the Father loves the Son. All should honour the Son just as they honour the Father (John 5:19–23).

The Son lived in complete dependence on the Father, and we are called to live the same way. Place one trial that tires you into the Father's hands now: what do you want to teach me through this? Amen.
kids: Children, good parents sometimes correct us because they love us. Today accept their advice with a smile!

homily: Dear friends, Paul tells Timothy what to say to the rich: not to be haughty, not to set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches, but on God who richly provides us with everything for our enjoyment; to do good, to be rich in good works, generous and ready to share (1 Timothy 6:17–18).

In the Gospel, at a Pharisee's house, a sinful woman washes Jesus' feet with her tears, dries them with her hair and anoints them with ointment. Jesus says: her sins, which were many, have been forgiven; hence she has shown great love (Luke 7:47). Her true treasure was her broken heart.
Those who are forgiven much love much. Today is the First Friday; this week experience the joy of forgiveness in a good confession, and let that love flow out in a generous gift. Amen.
kids: Children, the woman cried and loved Jesus, and Jesus forgave her. Tonight tell Jesus: sorry, and I love you.

homily: Dear friends, the Church in Corinth was splitting into parties: I belong to Paul, I belong to Apollos, I belong to Cephas, I belong to Christ. Paul's answer is sharp: has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified for you (1 Corinthians 1:12–13)?
In the Gospel some Greeks who came up for the feast ask Philip: sir, we wish to see Jesus (John 12:21). This is what the world wants from us: not our parties, but to see Jesus.

Today the Church remembers the 33 martyrs of Melitene, who, tradition says, gave their lives together for the one Christ. This week take one step to heal a division in the parish or in the family; then others will see Jesus in us. Amen.
kids: Children, some people said: we wish to see Jesus. Let others see Jesus through your kindness!

homily: Dear friends, Paul's words to slaves may sound strange to us, but their core is clear: whatever our station, we serve so that the name of God and the teaching may not be blasphemed (1 Timothy 6:1). Our work is our witness.

In the parable of the labourers in the vineyard, the landowner calls workers early in the morning, at nine, at noon, at three, and even at five o'clock, and in the end gives all the same wage. Are you envious because I am generous, he asks (Matthew 20:15). God calls at every hour, and his generosity is greater than our calculations.

Today the Church remembers the prophet Samuel and Pope St Leo the Great. The boy Samuel said: speak, Lord, for your servant is listening (1 Samuel 3:10). At every age and at every hour, let this be our prayer. Amen.
kids: Children, the boy Samuel said to God: speak, I am listening. Say the same prayer tonight before you sleep.

homily: Dear friends, the temple in Jerusalem had a wall that kept Gentiles out of the inner courts. Paul says that on the Cross Christ broke down every such wall: he is our peace; he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall of hostility, reconciling both to God in one body (Ephesians 2:14–16).

In the Gospel Jesus speaks of newness: no one sews a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old cloak, nor is new wine put into old wineskins; new wine is put into fresh wineskins (Matthew 9:16–17). The new life Jesus brings does not fit inside old habits; it makes the heart new.

Is there still a wall standing in our heart: of caste, of Church group, of an old wound? We are one house, built on Christ the cornerstone. This week let us take one step of friendship towards someone who stands apart from us. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus broke down all the walls and made everyone one family. Today make friends with a child from another group!

homily: Dear friends, Paul prays that the eyes of the Ephesians' hearts may be enlightened, so that they may know the hope of their calling, the riches of their inheritance and the immeasurable greatness of God's power, the power that raised Christ from the dead (Ephesians 1:18–20). That power is at work in the Church today.

In the Gospel Jesus speaks of the seed that grows by itself: someone scatters seed on the ground, sleeps and rises night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows, he does not know how (Mark 4:26–27). The growth of the Kingdom is not in our control; we sow, God gives the growth.

Today the Church remembers St John the Almsgiver, Patriarch of Alexandria, who called the poor my masters. Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the Lord. Today sow one small seed of mercy; God will give the growth. Amen.
kids: Children, a little seed grows into a big plant even when we do not see it. God will make big even a small good deed you do today!

homily: Dear friends, Paul speaks of a wisdom not of this age, hidden and now revealed: if the rulers of this age had understood it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory. What no eye has seen nor ear heard, God has prepared for those who love him, and he has revealed it to us through the Spirit (1 Corinthians 2:8–10).

In the Gospel Jesus compares the Kingdom to treasure hidden in a field and to a pearl of great value; whoever finds it sells all he has with joy to buy it. Every scribe trained for the Kingdom is like the master of a household who brings out of his treasure what is new and what is old (Matthew 13:44–52).

Today the Malankara Church remembers St John Chrysostom, the golden-mouthed, a great Father whom all the Eastern Churches still treasure. He brought out of Scripture what is new and what is old. Let us seek this treasure every day too: ten minutes with the Bible today. Amen.
kids: Children, a man found treasure in a field and gave everything with joy to have it. Jesus is our greatest treasure!

homily: Dear friends, Paul asks to be regarded as servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries; and it is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy. He does not even judge himself; when the Lord comes, he will bring to light the things now hidden in darkness and disclose the purposes of the heart (1 Corinthians 4:1–5).

Today is the memory of Mar Philipose Shleeha, St Philip the Apostle. At the Last Supper Philip says to Jesus: Lord, show us the Father, and we will be satisfied. Jesus answers: have I been with you all this time, Philip, and you still do not know me? Whoever has seen me has seen the Father (John 14:8–9).

The face of the Father is in Jesus. Like Philip we too are sometimes close to Jesus without truly knowing him. Today, at the Holy Qurbono and in prayer, let us look at the face of Jesus: there we see the Father. Amen.
kids: Children, Philip said: show us God. Jesus said: whoever sees me sees the Father. When we look at Jesus, we see God!

homily: Dear friends, today is the memory of Mar Mathai Shleeha, St Matthew the Apostle. Matthew sat at the tax booth, a collaborator with Rome, despised by his people. Jesus looked at him and said two words: follow me. And he got up and followed him. That evening Jesus ate at Matthew's house with tax collectors and sinners: I desire mercy, not sacrifice; I have come to call not the righteous but sinners (Matthew 9:9–13).
Paul urges us to lead a life worthy of our calling, with all humility, gentleness and patience: one body and one Spirit, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all (Ephesians 4:1–6).

In this week after the Sunday of the Message to Zechariah we see whom God calls: an old priest, a tax collector. No one is too far away to be called. Today let us answer, here I am, and invite someone who has drifted away to our table. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus called Matthew whom everyone disliked, and ate at his house. Don't leave anyone out; Jesus loves everyone!

homily: Dear friends, Paul compares God's people to an olive tree. Some natural branches were broken off; the Gentiles, a wild olive shoot, were grafted in to share the rich root. So he warns: do not boast over the branches; it is not you that support the root, but the root that supports you (Romans 11:17–18).

In the Gospel some people bring to Jesus a paralysed man lying on a bed. Seeing their faith, Jesus says: take heart, son; your sins are forgiven. And so that they may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins, he heals him (Matthew 9:2–6). The faith of others carried him.

We too have been carried by the faith of others: our parents, our ancestors, the tradition of the St Thomas Christians. Today let us carry someone: a sick person, someone weary in faith, bringing them to Jesus in prayer. Amen.
kids: Children, friends carried a sick man to Jesus. Today pray for someone who is sick!

homily: Dear friends, the last lines of Paul's last letter are a list of names: Prisca and Aquila, the household of Onesiphorus, Erastus, Trophimus left ill at Miletus, Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, Claudia. The Lord be with your spirit; grace be with you (2 Timothy 4:19–22). The great apostle, near death, remembers his friends.

In the Gospel Jesus laments over Jerusalem: how often have I desired to gather your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing! You will not see me again until you say, blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord (Matthew 23:37–39).

God's love shelters like a mother's wings, but it does not force. Let us take refuge under those wings. Like Paul, let us remember our friends by name in prayer, and send someone a message of love today. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus wants to protect us as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings. Today pray for your friends by name!

homily: Dear friends, Paul turns to the Christian home: children, obey your parents in the Lord; honour your father and mother, the first commandment with a promise. And he tells fathers something revolutionary for the time: do not provoke your children to anger, but bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord (Ephesians 6:1–4).

In the Gospel Jesus warns against leaders who say but do not do. The greatest among you will be your servant; all who exalt themselves will be humbled, and all who humble themselves will be exalted (Matthew 23:11–12).

Faith is first learnt at home, more by example than by words. Parents, let your children see you pray and forgive. Children, thank your father and mother today. A family that walks humbly is a small picture of God's Kingdom. Amen.
kids: Children, honouring your father and mother is God's commandment. Today give them a hug and say thank you!

homily: Dear friends, Paul says salvation is not far away, as if we had to climb to heaven or descend to the abyss to fetch Christ. The word is near you, on your lips and in your heart. If you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved (Romans 10:8–9). Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.

In the parable of the sower the same seed falls on the path, on rocky ground, among thorns and on good soil; what fell on good soil brought forth grain, a hundredfold, sixtyfold, thirtyfold. Let anyone with ears listen (Matthew 13:3–9).

The word is near; the question is how open our heart is. This week let us call on the name of Jesus in our heart throughout the day: Lord Jesus, have mercy on me. That short prayer turns the heart into good soil. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus saves everyone who calls on his name. Today say many times in your heart: Jesus, I love you.

homily: Dear friends, the short letter to Philemon begins with warmth. Paul, a prisoner, thanks God for Philemon's love and faith: the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, my brother (Philemon 7). The very presence of some people is a comfort to others.

In the Gospel Jesus says: no good tree bears bad fruit; each tree is known by its own fruit. The good person out of the good treasure of the heart produces good, for it is out of the abundance of the heart that the mouth speaks (Luke 6:43–45).

Today the Church remembers Pope St Clement and St Felicity, trees that bore fruit. Our words reveal our heart. Today speak one word that refreshes someone's heart: a thank you, an encouragement, a blessing. Amen.
kids: Children, a good tree gives good fruit; a good heart speaks good words. Say three kind words to others today!

homily: Dear friends, Titus 2 is read at Christmas in many Churches: the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all (Titus 2:11). In the child of Bethlehem God's kindness took a human face. That grace is also a teacher: it trains us to renounce impiety and worldly passions, and to live self-controlled, upright and godly lives.

In the Gospel Jesus tells us to learn from the fig tree: as soon as its branch becomes tender and puts forth its leaves, you know that summer is near. Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away. About that day and hour no one knows but the Father (Matthew 24:32–36).

In the season of Annunciation we prepare for two comings: the memory of his coming at Bethlehem and the hope of his coming in glory. We do not need to calculate dates; we need to be ready. This week, for one moment each day, let us say quietly: come, Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, the birthday of baby Jesus is coming! Start planning today to make a crib at home.

homily: Dear friends, Paul is in chains, and some preachers are using his imprisonment to make themselves look better. His reaction is astonishing: what does it matter? Just this, that Christ is proclaimed in every way, and in that I rejoice. My hope is that Christ will be exalted now as always in my body, whether by life or by death (Philippians 1:18–20).

In the Gospel Jesus tells his disciples: blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear. Many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see, but did not see it (Matthew 13:16–17).

We have been given the blessing the prophets longed for: to know Christ. That is greater than our own reputation. Today let us rejoice whenever Christ is proclaimed, even through others, and give thanks instead of being jealous. Amen.
kids: Children, when someone else does well, be happy instead of jealous. Praise a friend today!

homily: Dear friends, Paul warns the Corinthians to flee from idolatry, and gives a reason that is pure Eucharistic theology: the cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a sharing in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not a sharing in the body of Christ? Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body (1 Corinthians 10:16–17).

In the Gospel Jesus teaches with authority in the synagogue at Capernaum; a man with an unclean spirit cries out: I know who you are, the Holy One of God. Jesus drives it out with a word, and all are amazed: what kind of utterance is this (Luke 4:33–36)!

It is the Holy One of God whom we receive at the Holy Qurbono. Those who share the one cup cannot serve other masters: money, power, superstition. This Sunday let us come to church a moment early and prepare our hearts in silence. Amen.
kids: Children, at the Holy Qurbono Jesus gives himself to us. On Sunday sit quietly in church and talk to Jesus!

homily: Dear friends, some Thessalonians, expecting the Lord's return at any moment, had stopped working and were living as busybodies. Paul reminds them that he and his companions worked night and day so as not to burden anyone: anyone unwilling to work should not eat. Brothers and sisters, do not be weary in doing what is right (2 Thessalonians 3:8–13).

In the Gospel, when the Pharisees ask about divorce, Jesus goes back to the beginning: from the beginning of creation God made them male and female; the two shall become one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate (Mark 10:6–9).

Faithful work and faithful love: both are good preparation for the Lord's coming. Today do your work with joy; let husbands and wives say a word of thanks to each other; and let us pray for couples who are struggling in their marriage. Amen.
kids: Children, helping with small jobs at home is part of loving Jesus. Help your mother or father with one job today!

homily: Dear friends, Paul writes as a father, not a schoolmaster: though you might have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers. Indeed, in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel. I appeal to you, then, be imitators of me (1 Corinthians 4:15–16). The kingdom of God depends not on talk but on power.

In the Gospel Jesus compares the Kingdom to a mustard seed: when sown upon the ground it is the smallest of all seeds, yet it grows up and puts forth large branches, so that the birds of the air can make nests in its shade (Mark 4:30–32).

Today the Malankara Church remembers St Catherine. Our Church too began like a mustard seed, and after the reunion of 1930 it grew to give shade to many. Let us thank the spiritual fathers and mothers who handed on the faith to us, and let us become a father or mother in faith to someone. Amen.
kids: Children, a tiny mustard seed becomes a big tree. Jesus will make your little faith grow big too!

intro: Theme: “The Church: God's holy dwelling among us.”

Our liturgical year does not begin with Christmas but with the Church. Before we celebrate what God has done, we remember where he does it: in a people he has made holy and chosen as his home. Today we ask three questions: Where does God dwell? On what is that dwelling built? What does it ask of us?

points.h: God desires to dwell among his people
sub: In the desert God told Moses to set up a Tabernacle, and his glory filled it.
Solomon built the Temple; but when the people sinned, Ezekiel saw the glory of the Lord leave the house.
God did not give up: in Jesus the glory returned to dwell among us in human flesh, and through him in the Church.
q: Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
points.apply: Our parish church is not a hall; it is the house where God's glory dwells. Enter it with reverence.

points.h: The Church is built on the rock of faith in Christ
sub: Jesus asks: “Who do you say that I am?” Faith is a personal answer, not only a family custom.
Peter answers: “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God”, and Jesus builds his Church on this rock.
The Church stands firm not because we are strong but because Christ promised: the gates of Hades will not prevail.
q: See, I am laying in Zion a foundation stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation: “One who trusts will not panic.”
He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Simon Peter answered, “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.”
points.apply: This week, answer Jesus personally in prayer: “Lord, you are the Christ, my Lord and my God.”

points.h: We are living stones, shaped by God
sub: Solomon's Temple was built of stones already shaped at the quarry; no hammer was heard at the holy place.
God shapes us beforehand through Baptism, the sacraments, trials and the Cross, so that we fit together in his house.
Peter, who wanted a Christ without the Cross, was corrected: the stone must accept the chisel.
q: The house was built with stone finished at the quarry, so that neither hammer nor ax nor any tool of iron was heard in the temple while it was being built.
Like living stones, let yourselves be built into a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Accept the “chisel” in your life (a difficult person, a sickness, a correction) as God shaping you for his house.

points.h: A holy God sends a holy people
sub: Isaiah saw the Lord and heard: “Holy, holy, holy”; he knew his own sin and was purified.
Then God asked: “Whom shall I send?” and Isaiah answered: “Here am I; send me!”
A sanctified Church is a missionary Church: we are made holy in order to be light for others.
q: Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.
You are the light of the world. A city built on a hill cannot be hid.
points.apply: At the Sanctus of the Qurbono, sing “Holy, holy, holy” with Isaiah, and say in your heart: “Here am I; send me.”

concl: The Tabernacle, the Temple, the glory, the rock, the living stones: all point to one truth. God wants to live with us, and he has made us his home in Christ.
As the new liturgical year begins, let us love the Church as our mother, build it up with our lives, and let its light shine in our families and our land.
2026-11-01.resolve: Make one visit to the church this week outside Sunday, and pray for your parish, your bishop and the whole Church.

intro: Theme: “Renew the house of God, beginning with yourself.”

Last Sunday we celebrated the Church as God's holy dwelling. Today, Hudos Eetho, the Church asks to be renewed. Jesus enters the Temple, drives out the traders and speaks of a new temple, his own body. Renewal is not a new building or a new programme; it is a return to God.

sub: Jesus makes a whip and overturns the tables: he will not allow God's house to become a market.
At Sinai the people exchanged the living God for a golden calf; idols always creep into the house of God.
Our idols today: money, status, rivalry and noise in God's house, and the busy “trade” in our own hearts.
q: And they said, “These are your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt!”
He told those who were selling the doves, “Take these things out of here! Stop making my Father's house a marketplace!”
points.apply: Name one idol that crowds God out of your heart, and remove it this week.

sub: Solomon knew that no building could contain God.
Jesus says: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up”: he speaks of his body.
Through his body, crucified and risen, we meet God; in Baptism we become members of that body, the Church.
q: But will God indeed dwell on the earth? Even heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain you, much less this house that I have built!
Jesus answered them, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” … But he was speaking of the temple of his body.
points.apply: Before Holy Qurbono, remember: you are entering the body of Christ, and you will receive him into your own.

sub: Moses interceded and God relented; there is always a way back.
Isaiah invites: “Seek the LORD while he may be found.”
The risen Christ knocks at the door of a lukewarm Church; renewal is opening the door to him.
q: Seek the LORD while he may be found, call upon him while he is near; let the wicked forsake their way, and the unrighteous their thoughts; let them return to the LORD, that he may have mercy on them.
Listen! I am standing at the door, knocking; if you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in to you and eat with you, and you with me.
points.apply: Make a good confession before the Annunciation season advances.

concl: The Church is renewed when each of us is renewed. Jesus still cleanses the temple, not with a whip of cords now, but with his word and his sacraments.
Let us open the door to him, cast out our idols, and become again a house of prayer for all peoples.
2026-11-08.resolve: Spend ten minutes in silence in church this week, asking: “Lord, what must you cleanse in me?”

intro: Theme: “God hears our prayers, even when we have stopped hoping.”
The season of announcements begins with an old priest and his wife who had prayed for years for a child. Their story is the story of every family that waits, prays and is tempted to give up.

sub: Zechariah and Elizabeth were righteous and blameless, yet childless: holiness does not exempt us from sorrow.
Like Hannah in the Temple, they poured out their soul before the Lord year after year.
Faithfulness in waiting is itself a gift that God sees and honours.
q: I am a woman deeply troubled; I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but I have been pouring out my soul before the LORD.
Both of them were righteous before God, living blamelessly according to all the commandments and regulations of the Lord. But they had no children.
points.apply: Bring to God again the prayer you have almost stopped praying.

sub: Abraham laughed at the promise of a son in old age; Zechariah asked for a sign.
God's “yes” came in the Temple, at the hour of incense, in the middle of ordinary duty.
Zechariah's silence was not only punishment but a school: nine months of listening before he could speak again.
q: Then Abraham fell on his face and laughed, and said to himself, “Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old?”
Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you will name him John.
points.apply: Do your daily duties faithfully; God often speaks in the middle of them.

points.h: Preparing a people for the Lord
sub: John will turn hearts of parents to their children and make ready a people prepared for the Lord.
Like Ruth's loyalty, true faith commits itself: “your God shall be my God.”
This season asks each family to become a place where the Lord is expected.
q: Do not fear, for I am with you, do not be afraid, for I am your God; I will strengthen you, I will help you.
With the spirit and power of Elijah he will go before him, to turn the hearts of parents to their children … to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.
points.apply: Restore family prayer this week, even for ten minutes each evening.

concl: The God who heard Zechariah hears us. His timing is not ours, but his promise does not fail.
Let us wait like Elizabeth, listen like Zechariah, and prepare our homes for the coming of the Lord.
2026-11-15.resolve: Each evening this week, pray for one couple waiting for a child or for one family in sorrow.

intro: Theme: “Let it be with me according to your word.”
Today heaven and earth meet in a small house in Nazareth. God's plan, promised from the first pages of the Bible, waits for the free “yes” of a young woman.

sub: After the first sin God promised a woman whose offspring would crush the serpent.
Through the centuries the prophets cried: “O that you would tear open the heavens and come down!”
In the fullness of time God sent his Son, born of a woman: Mary is that woman.
q: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel.
But when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law.
points.apply: Thank God this week that he did not abandon humanity after sin.

points.h: Full of grace, by the power of the Spirit
sub: The angel greets Mary as the “favored one”: God's grace has prepared her.
The Incarnation is not human achievement but the work of the Holy Spirit overshadowing her.
God still works “not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit”.
q: Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, says the LORD of hosts.
The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the child to be born will be holy; he will be called Son of God.
points.apply: Before every important task, pray: “Come, Holy Spirit.”

sub: Mary asks how, not whether: her question seeks understanding, not proof.
She surrenders like clay to the potter: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord.”
Her “yes” changes history; our small daily “yes” lets Christ be born in our world.
q: Yet, O LORD, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you are our potter; we are all the work of your hand.
Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.
points.apply: Pray the Angelus (or three Hail Marys) every day this week, morning, noon and evening.

concl: God never forces his love; he asks. In Mary humanity answered “yes” on behalf of us all.
Let us learn from her to listen, to ask, and to say each day: “Let it be with me according to your word.”
2026-11-22.resolve: Say one hidden “yes” to God this week in something you have been resisting.

intro: Theme: “Carrying Christ to others.”
Mary has just said “yes” to God. Her first act is not to stay home in wonder but to set out in haste to help her elderly cousin. Where Mary goes, Christ goes, and the Spirit fills a home with joy.

sub: She goes “with haste” to the hill country: love does not delay.
At her greeting the child leaps in Elizabeth's womb, and Elizabeth is filled with the Holy Spirit.
Like Abraham's servant led by God to Rebekah's house, Mary is led to the home that needs her.
q: Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken his steadfast love and his faithfulness toward my master.

When Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, the child leaped in her womb. And Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit and exclaimed with a loud cry, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.”
points.apply: Visit someone who is old, sick or alone this week, and take Christ with you in your kindness.

sub: Elizabeth praises Mary first for her faith, not her privilege.
True beauty, says Proverbs, is the fear of the Lord.
Our families are blessed not by wealth or appearance but by faith lived together.
q: Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.
points.apply: Thank God for a woman of faith who formed you: mother, grandmother, teacher, sister.

points.h: The Magnificat: God lifts up the lowly
sub: Mary sings like Hannah before her: joy in God the Saviour.
God looks at the lowly; he scatters the proud and fills the hungry.
Mary's song is the song of the poor Church, and a call to serve the poor.
q: He raises up the poor from the dust; he lifts the needy from the ash heap.
My spirit rejoices in God my Savior, for he has looked with favor on the lowliness of his servant.
points.apply: Pray the Magnificat each evening this week.

concl: The Visitation shows the Church's mission: to carry Christ to every home, to serve with haste, and to sing God's praise.
May our visits, words and works make others' hearts leap with joy.
2026-11-29.resolve: Make one visit of charity this week, and pray the Magnificat with your family.

intro: Theme: “Blessed are the pure in heart.”
The Beatitudes as God's call to holiness.

sub: Holiness is not for a few; it is God's will for all.
It shapes how we live in the body and treat others.
q: You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.
For God did not call us to impurity but in holiness.
points.apply: Avoid one occasion of sin you know well.

sub: The psalmist asks who may stand in God's holy place.
Jesus promises the vision of God to the pure.
q: Who shall ascend the hill of the LORD? And who shall stand in his holy place? Those who have clean hands and pure hearts,
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
points.apply: Make a short examination of conscience tonight.

sub: The meek inherit the land.
The poor in spirit already have the kingdom.
q: But the meek shall inherit the land, and delight themselves in abundant prosperity.
Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
points.apply: Give way gently in one argument today.

concl: The Beatitudes are the face of Jesus.
Let his face appear in ours.
2026-11-02.resolve: Live one Beatitude each day this week.

intro: Theme: “The same yesterday and today and forever.”
The Fathers of Nicaea and the faithful servant.

sub: Faith comes to us through people.
We honour them by imitating their faith.
q: Remember the days of old, consider the years long past; ask your father, and he will inform you; your elders, and they will tell you.
Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.
points.apply: Pray for the priest who baptised you.

sub: Fashions in ideas come and go.
The Creed of Nicaea still confesses the same Lord.
q: For I the LORD do not change;
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
points.apply: Say the Nicene Creed slowly today.

sub: Moses was faithful in God's house.
The servant feeds others at the proper time.
q: Not so with my servant Moses; he is entrusted with all my house.
Who then is the faithful and wise slave, whom his master has put in charge of his household, to give the other slaves their allowance of food at the proper time?
points.apply: Do one duty today exactly and on time.

concl: We stand on the faith of the Fathers.
Let us be found faithful when the Lord comes.
2026-11-03.resolve: Learn the Nicene Creed by heart this month.

intro: Theme: “Forgive, and you will be forgiven.”
Humility before God, gentleness with others.

sub: Samuel was deceived by appearances.
Only God sees the heart; so we must not condemn.
q: for the LORD does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.
Do not judge, and you will not be judged; do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven;
points.apply: Pray for someone you have judged.

sub: Israel was warned not to boast of its wealth.
Paul asks the Corinthians what they have not received.
q: Do not say to yourself, “My power and the might of my own hand have gotten me this wealth.” But remember the LORD your God, for it is he who gives you power to get wealth,
What do you have that you did not receive? And if you received it, why do you boast as if it were not a gift?
points.apply: Name three gifts you did not earn.

points.h: The log in my own eye
sub: Ask God to search your heart.
Conversion begins with me.
q: Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my thoughts.
Why do you see the speck in your neighbor's eye, but do not notice the log in your own eye?
points.apply: Go to confession this month.

concl: The humble do not judge.
The measure we give is the measure we receive.
2026-11-04.resolve: Hold back one criticism every day this week.

intro: Theme: “The Lord disciplines those whom he loves.”
Sons and daughters in the Son.

sub: Proverbs already called correction a father's love.
Its fruit comes later: peace and righteousness.
q: My child, do not despise the LORD's discipline or be weary of his reproof, for the LORD reproves the one he loves, as a father the son in whom he delights.
Now, discipline always seems painful rather than pleasant at the time, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
points.apply: Accept one correction today without excuses.

sub: The psalm announces the Son of God.
Jesus does only what he sees the Father doing.
q: I will tell of the decree of the LORD: He said to me, “You are my son; today I have begotten you.”
Very truly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing on his own, but only what he sees the Father doing; for whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise.
points.apply: Ask before each decision: what would the Father do?

sub: God shares his glory with no idol.
He shares it with the Son, one with him.
q: I am the LORD, that is my name; my glory I give to no other,
so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. Anyone who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him.
points.apply: Bow your head at the name of Jesus today.

concl: Trials are the Father's training.
In the Son we learn to be children.
2026-11-05.resolve: Thank God each night for one hard thing that shaped you.

intro: Theme: “She has shown great love.”
True riches and the tears of the forgiven.

points.h: Do not set your heart on riches
sub: The psalmist warns against trusting wealth.
Paul tells the rich to hope in God.
q: if riches increase, do not set your heart on them.

As for those who in the present age are rich, command them not to be haughty, or to set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches, but rather on God who richly provides us with everything for our enjoyment.
points.apply: Give something today to a person in need.

points.h: A broken heart at his feet
sub: God does not despise a contrite heart.
The woman weeps at Jesus' feet.
q: The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.
She stood behind him at his feet, weeping, and began to bathe his feet with her tears and to dry them with her hair.
points.apply: Spend five minutes before a crucifix.

sub: Scarlet sins become white as snow.
Faith saves and sends us in peace.
q: Come now, let us argue it out, says the LORD: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be like snow;
And he said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”
points.apply: Make a good confession soon.

concl: God sees love where others see sin.
Let mercy make us generous.
2026-11-06.resolve: Make one act of generosity every Friday.

intro: Theme: “Sir, we wish to see Jesus.”
Unity that points to Christ.

sub: Unity among brothers is good and pleasant.
Paul begs the Corinthians to end their divisions.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
Now I appeal to you, brothers and sisters, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you be in agreement and that there be no divisions among you,
points.apply: Speak kindly to someone you are estranged from.

sub: God's word never returns empty.
The Cross does not need our cleverness.
q: so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose,
For Christ did not send me to baptize but to proclaim the gospel, and not with eloquent wisdom, so that the cross of Christ might not be emptied of its power.
points.apply: Read the Sunday Gospel in advance.

sub: The psalmist longs to behold the Lord's beauty.
The Greeks ask Philip to see Jesus.
q: One thing I asked of the LORD, that will I seek after: to live in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD,
They came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and said to him, “Sir, we wish to see Jesus.”
points.apply: Invite one person to the Holy Qurbono.

concl: A divided Church hides Christ.
A united Church shows him.
2026-11-07.resolve: Pray daily this week for unity in your parish.

intro: Theme: “Not one of these little ones should be lost.”
God's rest and the shepherd's search.

sub: The psalm warns against hardened hearts.
God's rest is still open to us.
q: O that today you would listen to his voice! Do not harden your hearts, as at Meribah,
So then, a sabbath rest still remains for the people of God;
points.apply: Read the day's Gospel before checking your phone.

points.h: The angels of the little ones
sub: God commands his angels to guard us.
The little ones' angels see the Father's face.
q: For he will command his angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways.
Take care that you do not despise one of these little ones; for, I tell you, in heaven their angels continually see the face of my Father in heaven.
points.apply: Pray for the children of your family by name.

sub: Ezekiel's God seeks the strayed.
Jesus wants not one to be lost.
q: I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed, and I will bind up the injured, and I will strengthen the weak,
So it is not the will of your Father in heaven that one of these little ones should be lost.
points.apply: Call someone who no longer comes to church.

concl: God's heart goes after the one.
Let ours go with him.
2026-11-09.resolve: Visit or call one lapsed person this month.

intro: Theme: “The last will be first.”
The generous Lord of the vineyard.

sub: Seek the Lord while he may be found.
The owner calls workers even at the last hour.
q: Seek the LORD while he may be found, call upon him while he is near;
and he said to them, “You also go into the vineyard, and I will pay you whatever is right.”
points.apply: Answer one call of God you have been postponing.

sub: His compassion is over all he has made.
Envy closes our eyes to grace.
q: The LORD is good to all, and his compassion is over all that he has made.
Am I not allowed to do what I choose with what belongs to me? Or are you envious because I am generous?
points.apply: Thank God for a blessing given to someone else.

sub: Samuel answered as a boy.
In God's kingdom the last become first.
q: Now the LORD came and stood there, calling as before, “Samuel! Samuel!” And Samuel said, “Speak, for your servant is listening.”
So the last will be first, and the first will be last.
points.apply: Pray Samuel's words before you sleep tonight.

concl: God's call and God's reward are both grace.
Let us answer gladly.
2026-11-10.resolve: Offer your work each morning this week.

intro: Theme: “He is our peace.”
Walls broken, a temple built, hearts renewed.

sub: Isaiah names the child Prince of Peace.
Paul says Christ himself is our peace.
q: and he is named Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
For he is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall, that is, the hostility between us.
points.apply: Greet someone you usually avoid.

sub: God lays a tested cornerstone in Zion.
We are built on it into one household.
q: See, I am laying in Zion a foundation stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation:
So then you are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are citizens with the saints and also members of the household of God,
points.apply: Pray for a parish group you seldom think of.

sub: God does a new thing in the wilderness.
New wine needs new wineskins.
q: I am about to do a new thing; now it springs forth, do you not perceive it?
Neither is new wine put into old wineskins; otherwise, the skins burst, and the wine is spilled, and the skins are destroyed; but new wine is put into fresh wineskins, and so both are preserved.
points.apply: Choose one new spiritual habit for this liturgical year.

concl: Christ breaks walls and builds a home.
Let him renew us this year.
2026-11-11.resolve: Keep one small fast this week.

intro: Theme: “The seed would sprout and grow.”
God gives the growth; we sow and give.

sub: Rain and snow make the earth fruitful.
The seed grows while the farmer sleeps.
q: For as the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and do not return there until they have watered the earth, making it bring forth and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater,
The kingdom of God is as if someone would scatter seed on the ground, and would sleep and rise night and day, and the seed would sprout and grow, he does not know how.
points.apply: Hand over one worry to God tonight.

sub: The psalmist asks God to open his eyes.
Paul prays for the eyes of the heart.
q: Open my eyes, so that I may behold wondrous things out of your law.
so that, with the eyes of your heart enlightened, you may know what is the hope to which he has called you,
points.apply: Read Scripture for ten minutes today.

sub: Kindness to the poor is a loan to God.
St John the Almsgiver lived this.
q: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and will be repaid in full.
The earth produces of itself, first the stalk, then the head, then the full grain in the head.
points.apply: Give something to the poor in secret.

concl: Sow the word and the alms; God brings the harvest.
Pray to see with the heart.
2026-11-12.resolve: Set aside a weekly sum for the poor.

intro: Theme: “One pearl of great value.”
The kingdom worth everything.

sub: Wisdom is to be sought like silver.
The finder sells all in joy.
q: if you seek it like silver, and search for it as for hidden treasures
The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which someone found and hid; then in his joy he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.
points.apply: Give up one thing today that keeps you from God.

sub: No eye has seen any God besides the Lord.
The Spirit searches the depths of God.
q: From ages past no one has heard, no ear has perceived, no eye has seen any God besides you, who works for those who wait for him.
these things God has revealed to us through the Spirit; for the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God.
points.apply: Pray to the Holy Spirit before reading Scripture.

sub: God's word is a lamp.
The good scribe brings out what is new and what is old.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
Therefore every scribe who has been trained for the kingdom of heaven is like the master of a household who brings out of his treasure what is new and what is old.
points.apply: Read a page of a Church Father.

concl: Christ is the pearl.
Joy makes every sacrifice small.
2026-11-13.resolve: Read one homily of St John Chrysostom this month.

intro: Theme: “Whoever has seen me has seen the Father.”
Faithful stewards who look on Christ.

sub: God promised a faithful priest.
Stewards of mysteries must be trustworthy.
q: I will raise up for myself a faithful priest, who shall do according to what is in my heart and in my mind.
Think of us in this way, as servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries. Moreover, it is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy.
points.apply: Pray for your parish priest by name.

sub: God tests the mind and heart.
Do not judge before the time.
q: I the LORD test the mind and search the heart,
Therefore do not pronounce judgment before the time, before the Lord comes, who will bring to light the things now hidden in darkness and will disclose the purposes of the heart.
points.apply: Leave one judgment to God today.

sub: Moses asked to see God's glory.
Philip asked to see the Father.
q: Moses said, “Show me your glory, I pray.”
Philip said to him, “Lord, show us the Father, and we will be satisfied.”
points.apply: Spend five minutes before an icon of Christ.

concl: We are stewards, not owners.
In Jesus' face we see the Father.
2026-11-14.resolve: Look at Jesus in silent prayer each day this week.

intro: Theme: “Follow me.”
The call of Matthew and the call to unity.

sub: Isaiah offered himself.
Matthew got up and followed.
q: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
As Jesus was walking along, he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax booth; and he said to him, “Follow me.” And he got up and followed him.
points.apply: Do at once one good thing you have postponed.

sub: Hosea preferred love to burnt offerings.
Jesus came for sinners.
q: For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
Go and learn what this means, ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’ For I have come to call not the righteous but sinners.
points.apply: Show mercy to someone others avoid.

sub: Ezekiel saw a divided people made one.
Paul begs for humility and patience.
q: I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king over them all.
I therefore, the prisoner in the Lord, beg you to lead a life worthy of the calling to which you have been called, with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
points.apply: Be patient with one difficult person today.

concl: Jesus still calls from the tax booth.
Answer, and live worthy of the call.
2026-11-16.resolve: Read one chapter of St Matthew's Gospel each day this week.

intro: Theme: “Your sins are forgiven.”
Faith that carries, grace that grafts.

sub: Ruth would not leave Naomi.
Friends carried the paralytic to Jesus.
q: Where you go, I will go; where you lodge, I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God my God.
And just then some people were carrying a paralyzed man lying on a bed. When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.”
points.apply: Pray by name for someone who cannot pray.

sub: The Lord forgives and heals.
The Son of Man forgives on earth.
q: who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases,
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins
points.apply: Plan a confession before 1 December.

sub: The just flourish like an olive tree in God's house.
The root supports us; so do not boast.
q: But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God. I trust in the steadfast love of God forever and ever.
do not boast over the branches. If you do boast, remember that it is not you that support the root, but the root that supports you.
points.apply: Thank God for the faith you received from your forebears.

concl: Christ forgives and heals.
We live from his root, not from our merit.
2026-11-17.resolve: Make a good confession this month.

intro: Theme: “Under her wings.”
The tender, persistent love of God.

sub: The psalm promises shelter under God's wings.
Jesus longs to gather his people.
q: he will cover you with his pinions, and under his wings you will find refuge;
How often have I desired to gather your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!
points.apply: Bring one fear to Jesus and leave it there.

points.h: Blessed is the one who comes
sub: Israel sang it at the feasts.
We sing it at every Qurbono.
q: Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the LORD.
For I tell you, you will not see me again until you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.’
points.apply: Sing the Hosanna with attention at the next Qurbono.

sub: The priestly blessing of Aaron.
Paul's last blessing on Timothy.
q: The LORD bless you and keep you; the LORD make his face to shine upon you, and be gracious to you;
The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you.
points.apply: Bless your children or family tonight.

concl: God's love gathers, never forces.
Let us be willing.
2026-11-18.resolve: Pray each day for ten people by name.

intro: Theme: “The greatest among you will be your servant.”
The Christian home and Christian leadership.

sub: The commandment carries a promise.
Children obey their parents in the Lord.
q: Honor your father and your mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.
points.apply: Call or visit your parents today.

sub: Moses told parents to speak of God's words at home.
Paul tells fathers to raise children in the Lord.
q: Keep these words that I am commanding you today in your heart. Recite them to your children and talk about them when you are at home and when you are away, when you lie down and when you rise.
And, fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.
points.apply: Pray with your children tonight.

sub: God asks justice, kindness and humility.
The humble will be exalted.
q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
The greatest among you will be your servant. All who exalt themselves will be humbled, and all who humble themselves will be exalted.
points.apply: Do one household task without being asked.

concl: Authority is service.
The home is the first school of the Gospel.
2026-11-19.resolve: Pray together as a family every evening this week.

intro: Theme: “The word is near you.”
Confess, call, and be good soil.

sub: Moses said the word is in your mouth and heart.
Paul applies it to faith in the risen Lord.
q: No, the word is very near to you; it is in your mouth and in your heart for you to observe.
because if you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
points.apply: Say “Jesus is Lord” aloud in your morning prayer.

sub: Joel promised salvation to all who call.
Paul opens it to Jew and Greek alike.
q: Then everyone who calls on the name of the LORD shall be saved;
For, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.”
points.apply: Pray the Jesus Prayer during the day.

sub: Jeremiah: break up the fallow ground.
Jesus: the good soil bears much fruit.
q: Break up your fallow ground, and do not sow among thorns.
Other seeds fell on good soil and brought forth grain, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty. Let anyone with ears listen!
points.apply: Remove one distraction that chokes your prayer.

concl: God sows generously.
Let our hearts be good soil.
2026-11-20.resolve: Read the Gospel of the day every morning this week.

intro: Theme: “Whoever does the will of my Father.”
Mary given to God.

sub: Hannah gave Samuel to God.
Mary was wholly given to God and said yes.
q: For this child I prayed; and the LORD has granted me the petition that I made to him. Therefore I have lent him to the LORD; as long as he lives, he is given to the LORD.
Then Mary said, “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.”
points.apply: Consecrate your family to God through Mary.

sub: The psalmist carries God's law in his heart.
Jesus calls those who do the Father's will his mother.
q: I delight to do your will, O my God; your law is within my heart.
For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.
points.apply: Ask in prayer: Father, what is your will for me today?

sub: Zephaniah calls Zion to sing.
Paul: rejoice in the Lord always.
q: Sing aloud, O daughter Zion; shout, O Israel! Rejoice and exult with all your heart, O daughter Jerusalem!
Rejoice in the Lord always; again I will say, Rejoice.
points.apply: Replace one complaint with thanksgiving today.

concl: Mary belonged wholly to God.
With her we do the Father's will and rejoice.
2026-11-21.resolve: Pray the Hail Mary for your family each evening.

intro: Theme: “Out of the abundance of the heart.”
Good trees, good words, refreshing love.

sub: The just are like trees by streams of water.
Each tree is known by its own fruit.
q: They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season, and their leaves do not wither. In all that they do, they prosper.
for each tree is known by its own fruit.
points.apply: Ask: what fruit did my day bear?

sub: The springs of life flow from the heart.
The mouth speaks what fills the heart.
q: Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life.
The good person out of the good treasure of the heart produces good, and the evil person out of evil treasure produces evil; for it is out of the abundance of the heart that the mouth speaks.
points.apply: Speak no word of complaint today.

sub: A true friend loves at all times.
Philemon refreshed the hearts of the saints.
q: A friend loves at all times, and kinsfolk are born to share adversity.
I have indeed received much joy and encouragement from your love, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, my brother.
points.apply: Encourage a tired person today.

concl: A good heart bears good fruit.
Let our love refresh others.
2026-11-23.resolve: Say one word of encouragement every day this week.

intro: Theme: “The grace of God has appeared.”
Living between two comings.

sub: Isaiah saw light for a people in darkness.
Titus: grace has appeared for all.
q: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light;
For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all, training us to renounce impiety and worldly passions, and in the present age to live lives that are self-controlled, upright, and godly,
points.apply: Plan your Christmas fast today.

sub: Habakkuk: the vision will surely come.
We wait for the blessed hope.
q: For there is still a vision for the appointed time; it speaks of the end, and does not lie. If it seems to tarry, wait for it; it will surely come, it will not delay.
while we wait for the blessed hope and the manifestation of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Pray “Come, Lord Jesus” each night.

sub: Grass withers; God's word stands.
Christ's words will not pass away.
q: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God will stand forever.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
points.apply: Learn one verse by heart this week.

concl: Grace has come and will come again.
Let it train us now.
2026-11-24.resolve: Keep the Twenty-Five Days' Fast faithfully.

intro: Theme: “Blessed are your eyes.”
Joy that Christ is proclaimed; eyes that see.

sub: Isaiah praises those who bring good news.
Paul rejoices whoever proclaims Christ.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation,
What does it matter? Just this, that Christ is proclaimed in every way, whether out of false motives or true; and in that I rejoice.
points.apply: Praise someone else's good work today.

sub: The psalmist blesses God at all times.
Paul wants Christ exalted by life or death.
q: I will bless the LORD at all times; his praise shall continually be in my mouth.

It is my eager expectation and hope that I will not be put to shame in any way, but that by my speaking with all boldness, Christ will be exalted now as always in my body, whether by life or by death.
points.apply: Offer your body and health to God today.

sub: Isaiah foresaw people who look but do not see.
Jesus blesses the eyes of disciples.
q: Keep listening, but do not comprehend; keep looking, but do not understand.
But blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear.
points.apply: Pray over the Sunday Gospel slowly.

concl: Rejoice whenever Christ is proclaimed.
Use the gift of seeing.
2026-11-25.resolve: Read one parable each day this week and ask Jesus its meaning.

intro: Theme: “He commands with authority.”
The word that frees and the table that unites.

points.h: He spoke and it came to be
sub: God's word created the world.
Jesus' word astonishes the synagogue.
q: For he spoke, and it came to be; he commanded, and it stood firm.
They were astounded at his teaching, because he spoke with authority.
points.apply: Let one word of the Gospel command your day.

sub: The seraphim cry “Holy, holy, holy”.
The demon confesses the Holy One of God.
q: Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.
I know who you are, the Holy One of God.
points.apply: Sing the Qadishat Aloho with attention.

sub: Moses sealed the covenant with blood.
Christ's cup makes us one body.
q: Moses took the blood and dashed it on the people, and said, “See the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you in accordance with all these words.”
The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a sharing in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not a sharing in the body of Christ?
points.apply: Prepare carefully for your next Holy Communion.

concl: His word frees; his table unites.
Let us have no other lord.
2026-11-26.resolve: Make a visit to the Blessed Sacrament this week.

intro: Theme: “What God has joined together.”
Faithful love and faithful work.

sub: Genesis: the two become one flesh.
Jesus: let no one separate them.
q: Therefore a man leaves his father and his mother and clings to his wife, and they become one flesh.
Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.
points.apply: Pray for married couples you know.

sub: God promises a heart of flesh.
Jesus names hardness of heart.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
But Jesus said to them, “Because of your hardness of heart he wrote this commandment for you.
points.apply: Ask God to soften one hard place in your heart.

sub: The ant teaches diligence.
Paul urges perseverance in good.
q: Go to the ant, you lazybones; consider its ways, and be wise.
Brothers and sisters, do not be weary in doing what is right.
points.apply: Finish one neglected task.

concl: God joins; love perseveres.
A new heart makes faithfulness possible.
2026-11-27.resolve: Pray every Friday for families and marriages.

intro: Theme: “Like a mustard seed.”
Small beginnings and spiritual fatherhood.

sub: Ezekiel saw a sprig become a cedar.
Jesus sees a mustard seed become a shelter.
q: On the mountain height of Israel I will plant it, in order that it may produce boughs and bear fruit, and become a noble cedar. Under it every kind of bird will live; in the shade of its branches will nest winged creatures of every kind.
It is like a mustard seed, which, when sown upon the ground, is the smallest of all the seeds on earth; yet when it is sown it grows up and becomes the greatest of all shrubs,
points.apply: Do one small act of faith today.

sub: God comforts like a mother.
Paul became a father through the gospel.
q: As a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you;
For though you might have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers. Indeed, in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.
points.apply: Thank or pray for your godparents.

sub: Not by might nor power, but by God's Spirit.
The kingdom is not talk but power.
q: Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, says the LORD of hosts.
For the kingdom of God depends not on talk but on power.
points.apply: Pray to the Holy Spirit before any important task.

concl: God's kingdom grows from small seeds.
Let us sow and trust.
2026-11-28.resolve: Do one hidden good deed every day this week.

intro: Theme: “We have found the Messiah.”
St Andrew, the one who brings others.

sub: The psalm invites us to taste and see.
Jesus invites the disciples to come and see.
q: O taste and see that the LORD is good; happy are those who take refuge in him.
He said to them, “Come and see.”
points.apply: Spend fifteen minutes alone with Jesus today.

sub: The nations say: come, let us go up to the Lord.
Andrew brings Simon to Jesus.
q: Many peoples shall come and say, “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob;
He first found his brother Simon and said to him, “We have found the Messiah” (which is translated Anointed).
points.apply: Invite one person to the Holy Qurbono.

sub: God never forgets the child of his womb.
Paul labours until Christ is formed in his people.
q: Can a woman forget her nursing child, or show no compassion for the child of her womb? Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you.
My little children, for whom I am again in the pain of childbirth until Christ is formed in you,
points.apply: Pray daily for one person you want to bring to faith.

concl: Andrew found Jesus and brought his brother.
May Christ be formed in us this Christmas fast.
2026-11-30.resolve: Pray for one person by name every day of the fast.
